hazard: Unroadworthy and unsafe condition of tractors and trailers

reports.title: Jon-Paul Prigent: Prevention of Future Deaths Report

promises.quote: We note your report was sent to a number of bodies with an interest in this issue. This response will address matters that are within HSE's areas of responsibility as a regulator, and highlight where matters are more appropriately addressed by other organisations.
promises.summary: Acknowledge receipt and clarify HSE's remit

concerns.quote: Tractors and trailers driven on roads for 'agricultural purposes' are not subject to periodic independent vehicle testing
concerns.hazard: unroadworthy and unsafe condition of tractors and trailers

concerns.quote: Tractors and trailers driven on roads at below a speed of 25 miles per hour are not required to be fitted with safety features to prevent decoupling
concerns.hazard: independent and uncontrolled travel of the trailer

concerns.quote: Basic hitch hook and ring coupling systems for tractors and trailers are very simple and convenient for ease and speed of coupling and use on farms but present clear risk when used on public roads without safety features to prevent decoupling.
Tractors and trailers are increasingly large and carrying heavier loads due to farm consolidation and are correspondingly traveling further distances on public roads
concerns.hazard: inadequate safety arrangements for large and heavy agricultural vehicles

concerns.quote: other nations, particularly in the European Union, have introduced comparatively robust legislation regarding testing and safety measures/fittings
concerns.hazard: lack of comparable legislation in current jurisdiction

concerns.quote: the fitting of safety features to prevent decoupling is relatively low cost and that there have been previous voluntary schemes to encourage and incentivise these measures
concerns.hazard: underutilisation of low cost safety features

reports.title: Richard Ellis: Prevention of future deaths report

concerns.quote: there are no legal requirements for the servicing and maintenance of agricultural tractors which do not fall within the requirements of the Road Traffic Act 1988 and the associated regulations
concerns.hazard: agricultural tractors not covered by Road Traffic Act 1988

links.explanation: Both reports highlight the absence of mandatory periodic testing or servicing requirements for agricultural tractors and trailers used on public roads. This leaves vehicle roadworthiness to the discretion of owners, creating a shared safety gap.
links.earlier_quote: Tractors and trailers driven on roads for 'agricultural purposes' are not subject to periodic independent vehicle testing.
links.later_quote: there are no legal requirements for the servicing and maintenance of agricultural tractors which do not fall within the requirements of the Road Traffic Act 1988 and the associated regulations.
